messages.subject: Device and Software Question
parts:
Hopefully this okay, please delete if not appropriate.  I was curious if anyone on the listserv has moved away from pencil and paper and/or recorders to smartphones and applications for recording distance data. Obviously, keeping your head up and away from those cheater glasses (as I approach 40) would, in theory, increase detection probability of clusters or objects when conducting point count surveys.

 

Suggestions welcome. As an agency, we are possible moving to smartphones for data collection for all wildlife surveys.

 

Thank you in advance.

messages.subject: RE: Device and Software Question
parts:
Shaun,

Note this is not an advertisement, but I just wanted to give you some insight into what is being used in Texas.

You might check out schnuppconsulting.com. They have information on a wildlife research database that can be used for multi-species, distance sampling surveys, and is compatible with multiple platforms (handheld gps, smartphones, rangefinders, etc.). It was developed by Matthew Schnupp (Wildlife Biologist for King Ranch) in partnership with Caesar Kleberg Wildlife Research Institute. We have used it the last 3 years for helicopter-based, distance sampling surveys for bobwhites, as well as multi-species ungulate surveys. Our equipment set up utilizes a Trimble Juno 5b handheld and 2-Trimble Laser Ace 1000 rangefinders that are connected via bluetooth.

Best,

John


John Edwards
Ph.D. Research Assistant
Caesar Kleberg Wildlife Research Institute
Texas A&M University - Kingsville

Hi Shaun,

We have been using a device we call a "Geometer" to record time, declination angle, lateral angle and gps data when the user presses a button. The device will also record voice and video. It is connected by USB to a computer and 4 or more of them can be used on a single computer. It has worked very well for us on aerial cetacean surveys around Iceland and Greenland.

You can find out more here. I am not involved financially with the company, but have been involved in the development of the device and software.

http://geometer.pitemp.com/ 

Daniel Pike.

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Device and Software Question
parts:
We conduct line transect surveys for seabirds under the Eastern Canada Seabirds at Sea (ECSAS) program. For this, I created a Microsoft Access database that is voice-activated with Dragon Naturally Speaking. The observer dictates observations in a prescribed format using a headset and the utterance is decoded and data is entered into the various fields in the database allowing the observer to focus attention on the birds and not the screen/keyboard. A quick glance at the screen before accepting the record is all that is required.

The computer is also connected to a feed from the ship's navigation system or a consumer GPS so that position, speed, etc are also automatically recorded.

Dave Fifield
Environment and Climate Change Canada
